_source: mediainfo 26.05 (MediaInfoLib v26.05) and ffprobe 9.0.1. Structural columns confirmed by byte inspection (od). GROUND TRUTH: never edit these numbers to make a test pass.
_reading: expectedFrameCount is the value this API must return. Where mediainfo and ffprobe disagree, see docs/decisions.md D11 and docs/evidence/sample-ground-truth.html.

sample.mp3.notes: VBR, joint stereo, 44100 Hz, LAME3.100. Both tools agree.

cbr-128-stereo-bare.mp3.notes: No tags and no VBR header: the file is nothing but frames. Both tools agree.

cbr-64-mono-info.mp3.notes: TOOLS DISAGREE. mediainfo counts the Info metadata frame as audio; ffprobe and the Info header's own frame-count field both say 78. Mono, so the Info marker sits 21 bytes into the frame rather than 36.

cbr-192-stereo-id3v1.mp3.notes: 128-byte ID3v1 tail appended by hand; mediainfo reads its title, confirming the tag is well formed. Both tools agree.

_edgeCases: Files that are not well-formed MP3s. Kept apart from `files` because the reference tools disagree about them, and because a count is not the expected outcome for all of them.

truncated.mp3.notes: The first 20000 bytes of sample.mp3. 96 complete physical frames end at byte 19973; a 97th declares 261 bytes but only 27 are present. The three answers differ for understandable reasons: mediainfo reports the Xing header’s declared 6089 and so describes a file that no longer exists; ffprobe counts the incomplete 97th frame it began reading; this service counts only frames whose bytes are all present, giving 96 physical minus the Xing frame.

not-audio.wav.notes: A real WAV file produced by ffmpeg, used instead of synthetic junk so the rejection is tested against a genuine container with its own header. No frames means the endpoint answers 400 NO_FRAMES_FOUND rather than a count.
